A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same R4 study, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Existing content can be matched across the added appendix and resulting renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on six datasets, gradient-fragility measurements, and ablations of data availability, masks, weight decay, and model size.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline mask-corruption results in Appendix F and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The R4 objective, Rand-R4 sampling, Adv-R4 optimization, Cert-R4 interval bounds, and language adaptations are unchanged. Added explanations and runtime estimates do not alter the proposed procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use Decoy MNIST, Decoy DERM, Decoy IMDB, ISIC, Plant, and Salient ImageNet. The new appendix uses existing DecoyMNIST coverage and the same four mask-corruption types, without introducing a new task or environment.

E2.justification: Appendix F adds R3 and IBP-Ex to the DecoyMNIST mask-corruption comparison, which v1 presented only for Cert-R4. Table 1's comparator set is unchanged; IBP-Ex+Grad-Reg is clarified as another name for the existing IBP-Ex+R3 baseline.

E3.justification: The added baseline corruption analysis reports gradient fragility alongside worst-group accuracy, whereas v1's corruption panels reported accuracy only. This extends the evaluation design within the reused corruption setup; existing dataset construction, architectures, and experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix F and Figure 4 examine R3 and IBP-Ex under increasing mask misposition, shift, shrink, and dilation on DecoyMNIST. This supplies a focused comparative robustness analysis; the existing data-availability, mask-availability, weight-decay, and model-size ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same standard-deviation reporting and significance highlighting. v2 adds no run counts, seed information, confidence-interval definitions, or statistical-testing procedures; Figure 4 continues the existing shaded-band presentation.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds baseline corruption results showing declining accuracy and increasing gradient fragility, with nearly overlapping responses across corruption types. Numerical entries in Tables 1-4 and the plotted results in Figures 1-3 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds simple runtime derivations: Nk(Tf+Tb), 2Nk(Tf+Tb), and 2N(Tf+Tb) for Rand-R4, Adv-R4, and Cert-R4. The robustness propositions, proofs, and interval-arithmetic definitions are substantively unchanged, moving from Appendices G-I to H-J.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and discussion retain the same central claims about robust explanation regularization, three approximations, benchmark advantages, language applications, and effectiveness with limited annotations. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains the existing omitted IBP results through scalability limits, discusses Plant performance through large saliency regions and bound looseness, and adds limitations involving large models, sparse masks, and constrained computation. Appendix F also interprets baseline corruption behavior through weight regularization.

D1.justification: v2 adds forward/backward-pass counts and computational-cost estimates, and explicitly explains existing regularization coefficients and the PGD step-size parameter. Architecture listings, data-processing descriptions, language adaptations, and the code-access link remain unchanged; no measured timings or new numerical hyperparameter settings are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhang et al. (2024) on targeted activation penalties and Gowal et al. (2018) on interval bound propagation. The positioning against R3 and IBP-Ex remains intact. Consolidating the duplicate Wicker reference does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: The three approximation subsections are grouped under a new Section 4.2 overview, with limited explanatory additions and updated cross-references. Author order changes, and the new Appendix F shifts subsequent appendix labels. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the four-panel Figure 4 and reflows existing figures and tables around the expanded text. Two Figure 1 panels have border-only changes; their data are unchanged. Existing table structures and Figures 2-3 are retained.

improvement.justification: Figure 4 supplies baseline context missing from v1's mask-corruption study. Explicit explanations of omitted IBP evaluations, computational tradeoffs, and applicability limits improve transparency. These are useful but bounded gains: the new comparative analysis covers one existing dataset, while the main method, benchmark results, and robustness proofs remain unchanged.
